title: GenWave Persona Catalog Entry Metadata
description: The <slug>.meta.json shape (app repo SPEC F89.1, catalog-owned). additionalProperties is false: unlike the card, this document belongs entirely to the catalog, so an unrecognized field is a contributor mistake worth failing CI on, not a forward-compat concern.
$comment: `added`'s pattern ends in (?![\s\S]), a lookahead meaning 'no character follows' — a portable absolute-end-of-string anchor that means the same thing in Python re, ECMA-262 (the dialect JSON Schema nominally specifies, and what ajv/most other validators use), and .NET. Plain $ was rejected: in Python's re (which is what actually enforces this schema server-side, via the jsonschema library), $ also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a value with a stray trailing \n would slip through. \Z was also tried and rejected: it's Python-only — under ECMA-262, \Z is a literal 'Z' character (Annex B identity escape), so a \Z-anchored pattern would reject every legitimate value and only accept ones ending in a literal Z. (?![\s\S]) has neither problem in any of the three dialects.

added.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) this entry was added to the catalog. `format: date` alone is annotation-only in draft-07 by default (most validators don't enforce it without an assert-format flag), so `pattern` carries the shape enforcement — but pattern alone only checks digit counts, not calendar validity (e.g. '9999-99-99' matches it); tools/validate.py separately parses this value with datetime.date.fromisoformat to reject a shape-valid but non-existent date.
added.$comment: Calendar validity (a real date, e.g. not Feb 30) is enforced by tools/validate.py. Plausibility (a believable date, e.g. not 9999-12-31) is deliberately NOT enforced here or there — that's PR-review judgment, not a schema/tooling rule. No upper bound is added on purpose: it would have to be tied to wall-clock 'today', and this catalog's whole validation gate is deliberately clock-free (see tools/build_index.py's generatedAt, which is tree-derived, never wall-clock).
